questions.id: Assemble a digital circuit on an FPGA
questions.stem: What is the correct process for assembling a digital circuit on an FPGA?

choices.A: Translate high-level code into Verilog or VHDL, synthesize, place & route, and finally configure the FPGA.
choices.B: Directly program the gates and flip- flops using binary codes.
choices.C: Manually wire logical components together inside the FPGA fabric.
choices.D: Load a pre-assembled circuit from an online library without modification.

questions.solution: The correct process involves translating high-level code into hardware description languages (Verilog or VHDL), synthesizing the design, placing and routing logic elements, and finally configuring the FPGA with the resulting bitstream.
questions.explanation: B is incorrect because FPGA programming does not involve direct binary coding of gates. C is impractical as manual wiring inside the FPGA fabric is not practical. D may require customization for specific applications.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing B, thinking that FPGAs work like traditional logic boards where components are wired directly.

questions.id: Implement a finite state machine on an FPGA
questions.stem: What is the primary method for implementing a finite state machine (FSM) on an FPGA?

choices.A: Use a lookup table (LUT) to store all possible states and transitions.
choices.B: Manually create flip- flops and logic gates for each state and transition.
choices.C: Program the FSM using a hardware description language like VHDL or Verilog.
choices.D: Connect premade FSM blocks from an FPGA library without modification.

questions.solution: The primary method is to program the FSM using a hardware description language (HDL) such as VHDL or Verilog, which allows for automated synthesis and optimization by the FPGA tools.
questions.explanation: A is incorrect because LUTs are used internally but not directly for FSM implementation. B is impractical for complex FSMs due to manual effort required. D assumes premade blocks will always fit the desired FSM, which may not be true.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing A or B, underestimating the power and efficiency of HDL-based FPGA design.

questions.id: Configure an FPGA for high-speed data transfer
questions.stem: What is a crucial step in configuring an FPGA for high-speed data transfer?

choices.B: Increase the clock frequency to its maximum value.
choices.C: Reduce the number of logic elements to minimize power consumption.
choices.D: Disable all unused I/O pins to save resources.

questions.solution: Using a low- skew clock distribution is crucial for maintaining signal integrity and ensuring reliable high-speed data transfer in an FPGA.
questions.explanation: B can lead to timing violations and instability. C reduces performance, not necessary for high-speed transfers. D may save resources but does not directly impact data transfer speed.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing B or C, focusing on unrelated optimization goals.

questions.stem: What is a common technique used to debug an FPGA design?

choices.A: Visualize the logic signals using a digital oscilloscope.
choices.B: Add blinkenlights to indicate circuit activity.
choices.C: Use simulation and synthesis tools to test the HDL code before implementation.
choices.D: Manually inspect the physical layout of the FPGA for errors.

questions.solution: Using simulation and synthesis tools to test the hardware description language (HDL) code prior to implementation is a common technique for debugging an FPGA design.
questions.explanation: A can be used but is not a primary debugging method. B is impractical for complex designs. D is not feasible as physical inspection does not reveal logical errors.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing A or D, focusing on hardware-based debugging methods rather than software tools.

questions.stem: Which of the following techniques can be used to optimize FPGA resource usage?

choices.A: Use a single large block for all logic instead of smaller ones.
choices.B: Reduce clock frequency to minimize power consumption.
choices.C: Employ pipelining and parallelism in algorithms.
choices.D: Disable unused I/O pins to save resources.

questions.solution: Employing pipelining and parallelism in algorithms can optimize FPGA resource usage by efficiently utilizing hardware resources.
questions.explanation: A increases resource usage due to interconnect complexity. B does not directly optimize resources, only power consumption. D saves resources but does not necessarily optimize usage.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing A or B, focusing on unrelated optimization goals.

questions.id: Configure an FPGA for real-time processing
questions.stem: What is a key consideration when configuring an FPGA for real-time processing?

choices.A: Maximize the number of available LUTs.
choices.B: Use a high clock frequency without considering timing constraints.
choices.C: Implement pipelining and parallelism in algorithms to reduce latency.
choices.D: Minimize the number of I/O pins to save resources.

questions.solution: Implementing pipelining and parallelism in algorithms is key for reducing latency and enabling real-time processing on an FPGA.
questions.explanation: A, B, and D do not directly address the need for low-latency processing. A and B can lead to timing violations or inefficient resource usage, while D does not impact processing speed.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing A, B, or D, focusing on unrelated optimization goals.

questions.id: Program an FPGA with a precompiled bitstream
questions.stem: What is the process for programming an FPGA with a precompiled bitstream?

choices.A: Translate high-level code into Verilog or VHDL, synthesize, and generate a new bitstream.
choices.B: Load the bitstream file onto the FPGA using a JTAG interface or configuration tool.
choices.C: Manually program the gates and flip- flops inside the FPGA fabric.
choices.D: Connect premade circuit blocks from an FPGA library without modification.

questions.solution: Loading the precompiled bitstream file onto the FPGA using a JTAG interface or configuration tool is the correct process for programming with a pre-assembled design.
questions.explanation: A involves creating a new design, not loading a precompiled one. C is manual work that defeats the purpose of a precompiled bitstream. D implies no need for loading a bitstream, which is incorrect.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Common mistake: Choosing A or C, assuming that FPGA programming always starts from scratch.
